newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Baer sees above-average result in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Baer sees above-average result in 1997.

text.p: Swiss private banking group Julius Baer Holding said it expected an "above-average result" for 1997 due to favourable business in the first half and a 39 percent rise in assets under management since a year ago.
"Based on our current perspective, we therefore anticipate an above-average result and significant growth of consolidated profit in 1997," Baer wrote in a letetr to shareholders.

Baer said six-month net profit after minorities rose 62 percent to 107.5 million Swiss francs, boosted by 63 percent growth in trading income to 129 million and 45 percent higher commission and fees income of 216.2 million.
Assets under management grew 39 percent from the year-ago period to 78.3 billion Swiss francs.
"The growth rates achieved in the first half of 1997 cannot be extrapolated for the entire year," Baer wrote.

"We have expanded the assets under management disproportionately in the past six to 12 months -- also substantially in excess of our long-term plan -- which provides a very robust basis for future business," the group said.
